en.headline: Police arrest two men over fake and scalped BigBang tickets near Kai Tak
en.dek: Officers said one suspect sold six counterfeit tickets for about HK$10,000 while another hawked two tickets above face value on Sunday, and the organiser invalidated the scalped ones.
body: Hong Kong police arrested two men on Sunday in connection with the sale of tickets for the Korean band BigBang’s concerts at Kai Tak Stadium.

Plain-clothes officers from the Ngau Tau Kok division detained one man near Kai Tak Sports Park after he was found offering two tickets for that evening’s show at prices above face value. The concert organiser invalidated those tickets after being notified by police.

In a separate case, venue staff at the sports park reported concerns about six tickets during a handover. Officers arrested a 34-year-old man on suspicion of obtaining property by deception after he allegedly sold the counterfeit tickets, valued at about HK$10,000, to a buyer. Police said the case was being handled by the Sau Mau Ping district crime unit.
Police urged the public to buy concert tickets only through official channels to avoid losses from fake or invalid passes.

zh.headline: 警方拘捕兩男 涉在啟德售賣BIGBANG演唱會假票及黃牛票
zh.dek: 警方指一人涉嫌以約一萬元售出六張假門票，另一人則以高於面值價格兜售兩張門票，主辦方已將涉案黃牛票作廢。
body: 香港警方周日在啟德體育園一帶拘捕兩名男子，涉嫌涉及韓國組合BIGBANG演唱會門票的非法買賣。
牛頭角分區便衣警員在啟德體育園附近，拘捕一名男子，指他涉嫌以高於門票面值的價格，兜售當晚演唱會的兩張門票。主辦方接獲通知後，已將該兩張門票作廢。
另外，場地職員在門票交收過程中發現六張門票有問題並報警。警方拘捕一名34歲男子，涉嫌以欺騙手段取得財產，指他向買家出售約值一萬元的六張虛假門票。案件交由秀茂坪警區刑事調查隊跟進。
警方呼籲市民透過正規渠道購買演唱會門票，以免因購買假票或無效門票蒙受損失。
